people.paul.role: Writer who leaves Titus on Crete to set things in order
people.paul.meaning: Paul says he left Titus on Crete to appoint elders in every city. He lists what an elder must be. He warns of deceivers who overthrow whole houses. He tells Titus to reprove them sharply. He then asks Titus to meet him at Nicopolis.
people.jesus.role: Savior whose grace and gift are the reason for good work
people.jesus.relations: Paul calls him Savior and our great God and Savior. Paul says he gave himself for us.
people.jesus.meaning: Paul says Jesus gave himself to redeem us from all iniquity. He says God saved us through mercy, and not by our works. Paul then asks his people to keep up good works.
people.titus.role: Paul’s true child, told to appoint elders on Crete
people.titus.relations: Paul calls him his true child in a common faith. Paul asks him to come to Nicopolis.
people.titus.meaning: Paul left Titus on Crete to appoint elders and set things in order. Paul tells him to teach each group what fits sound doctrine. Paul tells him to remind them to do good works. Paul asks him to come to Nicopolis once Artemas or Tychicus arrives.
people.tychicus.role: Worker Paul may send to Titus
people.tychicus.relations: Paul says he will send Artemas or Tychicus to Titus.
people.tychicus.meaning: Paul says he will send Artemas or Tychicus to Titus. Then Titus is to come to Paul at Nicopolis. The letter does not say which of the two Paul sends.
people.apollos.role: Traveler Titus must send on his journey
people.apollos.relations: Paul names him with Zenas the lawyer.
people.apollos.meaning: Paul tells Titus to send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey. He must do it quickly. Nothing may be lacking for them.
places.crete.summary: Paul left Titus on Crete in chapter 1. Titus is to appoint elders in every city there. Paul warns him about deceivers on the island.
places.crete.limits: Crete is an island. The letter names no town or meeting place on it.
sources.web.summary: The full Scripture text is the main text for original close readings.
sources.web.limits: Paul is the named writer. The guide did not check authorship, dates, Greek forms, or manuscripts. It did not check claims about whole peoples. It did not check the full travel plan. The quoted insult is not independent evidence about every Cretan. Nicopolis has no secure location here.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-44.summary: The lesson links sound doctrine with protection from false teaching.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-44.limits: Titus coverage follows what the lesson discusses in chapters one and two. The title alone does not show coverage of chapter three or Philemon. The guide did not check the linked Restoration passages.
sources.pietz-titus.summary: Pietz reads grace as the reason for changed conduct and good work.
sources.pietz-titus.limits: This is Pietz’s own reading. The guide did not check her Greek analysis, authorship, or social claims about Crete. It did not check household codes or the books she cites.
sources.net-crete.summary: The dictionary names Crete as an island and gives map coordinates.
sources.net-crete.limits: Only the opening place description and the coordinates support the island marker. The guide did not check the old history or the ethnic stereotypes. It did not check the towns or the travel order.
chapters.*.mapNote: Where Crete appears, the map marks it as one island point. Nicopolis has no point.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The letter gives no travel route.
